questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try something new, and see psychology in a totally different part of the world :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Oh wow, it definitely took some help. The Global Service Center at Korea University were amazing at helping, and had orientation and always answered questions and emails within one day.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Well, the university helped a lot, by making us buddy groups (like tutors) and social help like that. Global Service center also gave us a very good guide book, with introduction and guides to both university life and also immigration etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Definitely. I recommend finding something in Anam, which is the area the university is, which is super charming, and there is lots of housing affordable for students. I lived with Simple Spaces, which I highly recommend., although you can definitely find it cheaper. I lived in their Korea University apartment, but I would recommend living more central than that! 

also, I lived in an area, where the metro did not go to. I wish I had lived somewhere, where I could walk to a metro stop. So i recommend that. With that being said, the transportation system is super easy (get a climate card, and fill it every month, so u can go anywhere), so it really wasn't a big deal, it just took time to take the bus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can find it cheaper, and generally living in seoul is cheaper than in Copenhagen!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It just took time, be patient <3 I had an ongoing to do list with a Korean flag on it, because there was always something to do.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It's kind of hard to remember now, but it was a lot of documents and a fee etc. But it all worked out, it just takes time to fill out. I was very stressed out about it, but luckily it was all online. 

For visa, it was annoying that I had to prove how much money I had, but I just borrowed some and sent it back, to send them the screenshot. It all worked out. 
It feels like a lot of back and forth, but it is all worth it in the end. 

Also note, that for the VISA you have to give them your passport for 3 weeks during summer! That almost fucked me up haha! But you can go talk to them if you need it anyways, they were super nice.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Honestly, not much. Did it myself. Just takes a lot of investment and time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 5/6 classes, and course registration in the beginning was definitely the most stressful time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I HIGHLY RECOMMEND e-mailing the professors of the classes that you want PERSONALLY WAY BEFORE COURSE REGISTRATION! Because they DO have power over who gets their class. And I DID NOT do this, which I highly regret, because other people did it before me they got the class before I did, which resulted in a ton of stress for me. It all worked out though luckily. 

Also, when the day of the course registration happens (it is like clicking and getting concert tickets) go to a PC Bang (like a computer gamer place) and use their high speed computers. It helped me, and also was a fun experience. Even though I didn't get even half of my courses at that time, it all sorted itself out in the end. So put ice in your stomach! Your exchange won't come crumbling down because of course registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
It was not harder, there was just more work during the semester, which scared and surprised me at first. They also have a different respect for the professors, so I was kind of scared to talk to the professors in the beginning, but they were of course all really nice, and I wish I had asked them more questions during the semester sooner. 

In general the cognitive courses I took were pretty high level, but the professors also seemed to be kind of famous and knew a lot of people in the fiels? I actually don't understand that no one else has gone to Korea University before for psychology, I think they really have some cool professors and thinkers there, also for New Media psychilogy and cultural psychology classes with lots of discussion and nuance.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More assignments, more monitoring of people's learning, more obligatory participation that counts for your grade. Midterms and end exams. It reminded me more of high school, but in general I actually really learned a lot. 

Group work was consistently a challenge throughout the semester - my impression was that people don't want to meet up and actually do the work together, which frustrated me through zoom calls and texts etc. We had plenty group presentations and assignments in general.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Learning and Memory 
Cognitive Neuroscience 
Behavioral Economics 

New Media Psychology 
Cultural Adjustment and Exchange
 Popular Culture and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Learning and Memory (was super hard in the beginning, but I ended up LOVING this class. I learned a lot about super detailed leanring and memory cognitively) 
Cultural Adjustment and Exchange (super cool prof, and cool texts. definitely high work load, but high pay off as well) 
I wanted to take Media and Gender, but couldn't fit it in the course plan...

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The obligatory health insurance that you have to pay every month for Korea (NHIS), you get a letter in the mail, it is 350kr pr. month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less, phone was more. transportation was less. In general, everything is less expensive than København (its really amazing, I had the best time)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
KUBA (Korea University Buddy Assistants) made basically everything available from bars and clubs to sports events restaurants, specific foods and places to go etc. Just ask them.
https://www.instagram.com/koreauniv_kuba_official/?hl=da

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There was a great language exchange club called LECA, but most clubs were closed for foreigners.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Seoraksan for hiking. Go to Yang Yang beach for surfing. Go to Busan. I didn't go to Jeju 
You can use Agoda for transportation to these places. If transportation is hard to figure out, ask someone in your class! They are shy, but they will help you.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy! Korea University made it very easy I think! But I mean still weird and crazy in the beginning of course. But don't worry.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You can do it! Go to the lanugage exchange group. Ask buddies to go to lunch and coffee with you. And class mates as well! I was nervous to sit by Korean students in the beginning, but ended up making friends with a couple by forcing myself to sit with them hahaha. And asking for how to get online books etc. And group work!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their shyness for sure. Not being able to speak the same language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Omg the going out to eat, karaoke rooms, the quietness in the transportation, ugh everything, I miss it so much.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. ENJOY OMG IT GOES BY SO QUICKLY - JUST DO IT!!! 
2. it's okay to take down time... and relax and just be. just sit and watch, just walk around. It doesnt have to be sight seeing everyday - I ended up enjoying my everyday life the very most. 
3. sign up for a hobby, like i took dance classes with some friends, do martial arts or fitness or something right away. get that everyday life going!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Haesong Law Library is the very best place to study...... Take a long walk around campus!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from around the world (through KUBA and through simple spaces)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: all the beurocratic stuff. I lost my wallet and had to go to the immigration office a million times because of it. So annoying. Bring an extra card from ur bank at home!!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
